brf2Suffix.doc: mission_brf2_load: appended to the scenario name's first 4 letters (yellscn1 -> yellbrf2)

optionLaunchAnim.doc: String constants the handoff code copies (xrefs in prm_save, star_set_member, star_launch_prepare).

mainProject.doc: project_open: the handle res_cache_proj_handler returns for MW2.PRJ; every cache_load_resource from the project passes it (MW2's mainProject)

inputDeviceCapacity.doc: S8 port: how many InputDevice records inputDevices has room for - input_devices_grow adds 50 (0xcb2 bytes) and returns it, input_devices_load grows when inputDeviceCount passes it, input_devices_free zeroes it.

chunkTags.doc: The BWD chunk tags packed 4 bytes apart, from 'BWD' up to briefingTags (which continues the same run): BWD, REV, DTBL, PLNT, ... BMPJ (+0x38), BMID (+0x3c), ... GPS (+0xd0). bwd_build_begin copies BWD/REV/DTBL from here, instmap_write BMPJ/BMID, star_bwd_add_mech GPS.

enemySkillTable.doc: Right after briefingTags: 9 rows of 5 shorts, indexed by skill in star_bwd_add_mech and copied to GPS +0x10 (MW2's gpsParams[0..4]).

opponentStarSkill.doc: mission_brf2_load: the second SDSC chunk's +8, the opponent star's skill. star_files_write starts the enemy files' skill rows at this - 2.

insigniaNames.doc: instmap_write: the six Clans' insignia bitmap names (l1wolfcl, l1jadefn, l1gostbr, l1smojag, l1novact, l1steelv). Indexed by its two arguments; each name is looked up in TABL 8 and written as a BMPJ. The -1 after them (0x7a820) is not a terminator: it is controlsSelectedControl's initial value (a 7-entry array here made controls.c read it as insigniaNames[6]).

controlsSelectedControl.doc: the selected cell: a control (-1 none) and its column (0 input, 1 input2)

controlsDevice.doc: the device whose axes and buttons the right-hand lists show

controlNames.doc: display names ('Throttle ' .. 'Next Nav Point', 6 empty) and the sim's names for temp.map ('throttle', 'legs_pan_delta' .. 'advance_nav')

controlsKeyboardDevice.doc: S8 port: the keyboard's device number. controls_screen sets it to -1 (the image's value), then to the index of the device named 'keyboard' ('Error: keyboard.dll not found' while still < 0); controls_write_temp_map's fixed legs_pan_minus / legs_pan_plus lines (GreyDelete, GreyPageDown) are bound to that device.

modifierNames.doc: indexed by flags & 7, which only takes 0, 1, 2, 4 (index 3 is '~--' too)

controlsDevicePanel.doc: controls_screen: the device-selection panel (20 rows) and the GAME CONTROLS binding panel (168 rows), both widget_panel_layout tables.

creditsLines.doc: credits_screen's lines: '<' heading, '>' job title, '~' heading (the date check's replacement), else a name; NULL is a blank line.

difficultyNames.doc: ---- options (S8) ---- options_draw_difficulty: label_create_under(font27, ..., [0x7d090 + byte * 4]) - '~EASY', '~MEDIUM', '~HARD' for simOptions.difficulty 0..2. Nothing bounds the byte: 3 would read optionsWidgets' first dword (x = 393) as the pointer.

midiEnabled.doc: Set by sound_system_init's caller: gates AIL_install_MDI_INI and main's music. main clears it (with 0x7d380/0x7d384) unless argc is 2.

digitalSoundEnabled.doc: The other start-up switches: each 1 in the data, and all cleared by main unless the shell was started with one argument (MECH2's way).   digitalSoundEnabled: sound_system_init keeps the digital driver for effects     only while it is set.   movieSoundEnabled: main sets the Smacker open flags (0x91194) to 0xfe00 - the     shape of Smacker's audio-track bits - when it is set, else 0; and     sound_system_init clears it when the digital driver cannot be installed. So     presumably movie audio; the Smacker flag values are not checked here.   simLaunchEnabled: main's state 10 runs the sim only while it is set.

moviesEnabled.doc: movie_play does nothing (returns 0) unless it is set; 1 in the image, and no writer found. main also tests it once at start-up (clib_sub_04b794).

cdPath.doc: 'X:\' - the CD drive's letter first (MSCDEX), '\0' without one; movie_play and the anim openers prefix it for 'X:\smk\name.smk'.

clanNames.doc: Indexed by PilotRecord.career in hall_of_honor_screen: Wolf, Jade Falcon, Ghost Bear, Smoke Jaguar, Nova Cat, Steel Vipers. Only 0 and 1 occur in the registry.

tabStops.doc: text_label_type_char's \T: the pen moves to the first of these past its offset from the label's x - 0, 36, 72 ... 612, then 640 (19 ints; the loop stops at 0x4c bytes).

archiveNames.doc: screen_archive: (&archiveNames)[career], the archive archive_page_load opens - ARCHWO.MW2 (Wolf), ARCHJF.MW2 (Jade Falcon).

formationTitles.doc: grievance_draw_formations reads entry formation * 2: the display names 'Echelon Left' ... 'Wedge'. The odd entries (0x7d4b4, 0x7d4cc ... then 0x11d) are not read by it; what they are is not established.

careerButtonsWolf.doc: The button tables those rows point at (listing/screen_buttons.txt, per career).

grievanceButtons.doc: screen_grievance's button_bar_create(..., 0x7e8a4, 0x19): 0 LAUNCH, 1 EXIT, 2 the next scenario, then two mirrored panels (3..13 the player's star, 14..24 the opponent's): member + (3..5 / 14..16), formation +, member - (7..9 / 18..20), formation -, insignia, MECH LAB, STAR CONFIG. Buttons 3..5 and 14..16 also give the member labels' positions (their labelX / labelY).

shellMenuItems.doc: shell_menu's six labels: NEW ALLEGIANCE, COMBAT VARIABLES, COCKPIT CONTROLS, HALL OF HONOR, THE KESHIK, FLEE TO DOS.

planetAnims.doc: mission_brf2_load's PDSC branch: anim_start(0, planetAnims[briefingPlanet * 2], 414, 10, 0x42, 0) - aplan01 .. aplan12. The odd entries, aplan01c .. aplan12c, are what screen_grievance starts in slot 0 (flags 0x4a) whenever that slot is not running.

grievanceScenarios.doc: Trial of Grievance scenarios: 10 names and a NULL (jackscn1 ... swisscn1). screen_grievance steps prmBlock.grievanceScenario through it, wrapping at the NULL, and loads the chosen one through pilots_sub_0291b0.

insigniaAnims.doc: screen_grievance's insignia animations, indexed like insigniaNames (wiawolf, wiajf, wiaghost, wiasmoke, wianova, wiasteel): slot 1 at (13, 205) and slot 2 at (483, 329).

grievanceChassisLimit.doc: screen_grievance: the mech-lab chassis count the member steppers wrap at, set on entry from star_record(0)->members[0].pilotName: Enzo 18, Hobbes 17, Calvin 16, else 15 (grievance_chassis_count computes the same for screen_mechlab).

equipmentNames.doc: {code, name} x 23, the equipment names (5000 MASC ... 9000 Ferro-Fibrous); mechlab_draw_slot finds a code by code / 50.

locationNames.doc: Head, Right Torso, Center Torso, Left Torso, Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, Left Leg - the mech lab's location names, MW2 section order.

structureTable.doc: BattleTech's internal structure table, one row per 5 t from 10 to 100 t (row (tons - 10) / 5): centre torso, side torso, arm, leg. The loader fills designLocations[].internal from it (head fixed at 3).

engineTable.doc: {rating, mass (hundredths of a ton), maker} per 5 points of rating, 10..400.

itemTypes.doc: The item types (weapons first): 0x28 bytes each, indexed by item id / 100. Typed for the 28 weapon types the WEAPONS TABLE can list (0..27); the equipment ids go further, but where the table ends is not established.

locationMarkerX.doc: mechlab_show_location_marker's offsets for animation slot 12, per location.

mechlabChassisCount.doc: How many chassis NEXT / PREV CHASSIS cycle through (0 .. count - 1): screen_mechlab sets 15 (Firemoth .. Dire Wolf), or in career 2 grievance_chassis_count's 16 / 17 / 18 for the pilot names Calvin / Hobbes / Enzo, which add the Elemental, the Tarantula and the Battle Master IIC.

mechlabChassis.doc: The chassis the mech lab shows (chassisTable index).

musicByStateGrievance.doc: Screen music (main). Per state, by career: 0 = leave the music alone, 0x20000000 = stop, 0x10000000 = restart, else a DATABASE.MW2 XMIDI base item (35..41) to which musicSetOffset is added.

launchAnimName.doc: mission_brf2_load copies the BRF2 stream's SUPS string here (the launch animation stem); prm_save appends it to MW2's command line after " -b=". 13 bytes: the image holds the 8.3 template "xxxxxxxx.xxx".

registerNextState.doc: screen_register: the result it returns, -1 until a button or shell_menu decides. A static at 0x8396c, not a local: set to 10 by a LAUNCH OLD MISSION row, 8 / 1 by the buttons, then tested once per pass.

registerPilotInfoPanel.doc: screen_register's two right-hand panels, drawn by widget_panel_layout.

midiDriverSets.doc: {char *mdiFile, int itemOffset} x 14: ADLIB.MDI 0, ADLIBG/OPL3/PASPLUS/SBPRO1/ SBPRO2/TANDY 8, SBAWE 16, MT32 24, MPU401/SNDSCAPE/ULTRA 32 (PAS, SBLASTER 0).

starSpriteFormatWolf.doc: screen_star_select points starSpriteFormat at one of these by career (0, 1, 2): star_slot_draw sprintfs the chassis's animCode into it for the member's sprite.

randSeed.doc: rand / srand (0x4bc39 / 0x4bc5d): the LCG state rand_state (0x4bc33) returns the address of; x = x * 0x41c64e6d + 0x3039, rand = bits 16..30. 1 in the image.

projectFiles.doc: project_set_alloc_hooks' two pointers (MW2's projectAllocHook / projectFreeHook): project_file_open and project_load_directories allocate through the first, project_file_close frees through the second The open-project records (seventy-fourth /shell-next): MW2's ProjectFile layout, matched field by field against the shell's project_file_open / _close / project_load_directories / project_resource_size / project_read_resource. Capacity 1: project_file_open only ever checks record 0's inUse, as MW2's does.

ordersTextRemap.doc: orders_text_build fills it on every call - [0] 0xff, [1] 1, [2..255] 0xff - and hands it to page_init as every briefing / debriefing line's colour table: only ink 1 draws.

bwdBuffer.doc: star_files' BWD build buffer (sixty-eighth /shell-next): bwd_build_begin clears it and appends the BWD, REV and DTBL chunks; every append checks bwdLength against 0x800 and raises bwdMaxChunk (mirrored into the header); the writers set streamLength = bwdLength and fwrite bwdLength bytes.

controlsEditText.doc: controls_edit_config_name's working copy of the text: up to 62 characters, the '_' cursor and a NUL. The space up to 0x8b0ec is not used by anything else found.

controlsSaveText.doc: controls_save_config's sprintf buffer: 'giddi\config%02d.cpc' for its fopen, then 'Configuration %d Saved.#Ok' for its message_box. 0x40 bytes, up to controlsMovie.

controlsMovie.doc: ---- controls screen (S8) ---- controls_screen's amwlogo1 loop: the 0x18-byte block it mallocs and hands to movie_open_background (0x73a86 'amwlogo1', at 120, 4), NULL when the malloc fails. Its steppers are controls_screen's two panel loops, controls_edit_config_name's key loop and controls_scroll_buttons' held-button loop; controls_screen closes and frees it. No other function reads 0x8b12c.

controlsRemapSelected.doc: controls_screen's two remaps: ink -> 0x10 for a chosen device, ink -> 7 for the devices that cannot be chosen once four are.

controlsCellText.doc: The binding cells' text: controls_draw_binding sprintfs '%s %s' (device, input) or strcpys '----' here, controls_draw_second_button sprintfs '/%s'; each hands it to label_create_under, which copies it. 0x100 bytes, up to controlsSelectedColumn.

controlDefaultsScratch.doc: controls_reset_defaults reads each device's giddi\<device>.cpc here

controlsDeviceRecords.doc: the .cpc's 16 device records: which device each saved binding number meant

controlsDeviceChosen.doc: per device slot 0..15: 1 when chosen (the keyboard always is)

controlsExit.doc: 1 leaves controls_screen (ACCEPT, ABORT, Esc); anything else after the device panel goes on to the binding panel.

optionsMovie.doc: shell_menu's COMBAT VARIABLES: the amwlogo1 movie_open_background it keeps stepping (zeroed before, left stale after its close); options_click_slider steps it too.

sliderShapes.doc: shell_menu's COMBAT VARIABLES: mpack_db_get_item(database, 8, &0x91154, ...); options_draw_slider draws shape 1 (the bar) and shape 0 (the knob) from it.

videoDriver.doc: main: the 0x3a6-byte video driver object (video_driver_sub_03dd90), which every font holder, page and label list is given. A pointer, kept as an int because every consumer passes it on as one.

uiFont.doc: Three more font slots (seventy-fifth /shell-next). main is their only writer (a sweep of every function's disassembly for stores to them), and all three end up holding the item-32 holder - 0x9116c first gets item 26's, like font32 - so at run time they are the same font as font32. Named by what reads them, which is consistent per slot: presumably the original kept one variable per role.   uiFont: label_create labels, button bars, message_box / menu text, text_input.     (message_box's decompile shows it being stored; that is a register reload     written back - the machine code only loads it.)   archiveFont: only ever passed to archive_page_load (the archive viewers and     the briefing's archive entries), which hands it to page_init.   pageFont: orders_text_build, page_init and text_width for the briefing and     debriefing pages and the honour lines.

database.doc: main: mpack_db_open(DATABASE.MW2); every mpack_db_get_item(database, item) - fonts, sounds, music, art - reads through it.

sound77.doc: main's four shared samples, by DATABASE.MW2 item (what each sound is, is not established beyond where it plays):   sound77  looping; every text page keeps it (text_markup, page +0x28) -            presumably the typing sound   sound101 the star screen's formation / starmate / CHANGE MECH buttons and            two mech-lab buttons   sound102 MECH LAB, the options slider preview, one mech-lab action   sound103 the archive holoprojector and archive pages

grievanceTextRemap.doc: screen_grievance's text colour table, filled on entry: the identity, 0 -> 0xff (transparent), ink 1 -> 0x22. Every member and formation label is drawn through it.

grievancePlayerFormation.doc: grievance_draw_formations: star_formation(0) / (1), stepped by buttons 6 / 10 and 17 / 21 and passed to star_configure.

grievancePlayerMembers.doc: screen_grievance: per member {TextLabel *, chassis index}, 3 per star. The chassis is what the steppers step (-1 none) and star_member_chassis refreshes.

planetLabels.doc: mission_brf2_load's PDSC branch keeps its three planet-description labels here (TextLabel *; label_destroy'd and replaced for each planet, through [ebp + 0xa2130]). screen_grievance zeroes them on entry, dropping the labels without destroying them. (The first note here said no reader had been found: a grep for the address missed the indexed access.)

briefingPlanet.doc: mission_brf2_load: PDSC's planet - 1 (0..11), which picks the aplanNN animation; screen_grievance clears it.

grievanceOpponentFormationLabel.doc: grievance_draw_formations: the two formation labels (TextLabel *) it replaces.

mekTons.doc: The MEK being edited: its header sits at 0xa22bc, six ints the loader clears together (memset 0x18). They follow MW2's MechChassis (tons, moveSpeed, jump, heatSinks, numWeapons, numAmmo; mw2_types.h), and the mech lab uses them that way: designMaxMass = tons * 100, heat sinks past 10 cost a ton each, jump jets are jump * a per-jet mass, rating = tons * walk.

mekNumWeapons.doc: The rest of the MEK record as mechlab_load_mek reads it and screen_mechlab's save writes it back (fwrite 0x18, 0x28 x 8, 8 x numWeapons, 8 x numAmmo, 50).

mekWeapons.doc: {slotCode, location} x 10; the loader copies slotCode into the weapon list

mekAmmoBins.doc: {binCode, weaponCode} x 25; binCode is what a section slot >= 10000 names, weaponCode seeds the design's ammo item

designTitle.doc: The variant's title, the MEK file's last 50 bytes: mechlab_load_mek copies the file's text here, a NEW variant sprintfs 'User Variant #%d' here (slot - 99), and the save copies it back into mekTitle and writes it. Where it is drawn is not traced.

designMaxMass.doc: The mech lab's design being edited, in HUNDREDTHS OF A TON: the loader (0x30db0) sets designMaxMass = the MEK's tonnage * 100, and the recompute (0x2eee0 and two copies) sets designMass to the sum of its parts and designFreeMass = max - mass. screen_mechlab's SAVE refuses max < mass.

designEngineIndex.doc: (rating - 10) / 5, plus 10000 when section 1 (right torso) holds code 5850 (the engine, MW2 damage callouts): an engine reaching a side torso is XL, and the recompute halves the table mass for it. Indexes the engine table 0x7f6cc.

designEngineRating.doc: The design's mass terms (hundredths of a ton), each summed into designMass by the recompute (0x2eee0). The name says how each is computed.

designGyroMass.doc: designEngineRating * 0.01 * 100, rounded up to a whole ton: rating / 100 tons rounded up, the BattleTech gyro (mechlab_remove_item_and_recompute). This was 'a whole-ton term, likely the gyro, unconfirmed' until that copy was read.

designCockpitMass.doc: always 300 (3 t), set by the recompute and added into designMass: the cockpit.

designHeatSinkType.doc: 1 single, 2 double: 'Single' / 'Double' in the HEAT SINKS panel, the critical slots each heat sink takes, and the factor the save puts on the MEK's heatSinks. (mechlab_load_mek's note left this as 'meaning not established'.)

designSlottedHeatSinks.doc: Heat sinks the engine cannot hold: count - rating / 25, at least 0. FASTER and SLOWER add or remove heat-sink items so this many need critical slots.

designEndoSteel.doc: designEndoSteel was named designStructureHalved (increment 31), for its one effect, before its writer was read: mechlab_load_mek sets it when any MEK section slot is 8001, and MW2SHELL's item table (0x7f4c4) names 8000 ENDO STEEL. The recompute halves the internal structure mass while it is set.

designFerroFibrous.doc: mechlab_load_mek sets it when any slot is 9001 (item table: FERRO-FIBROUS); armour then costs 1/19.2 t a point (0x76e3d) instead of 1/16 (0x76e2d), in the loader and in mechlab_trim_armour_to_tonnage.

designArmourAllocated.doc: Points actually spread over the locations (designLocations front + rear); mechlab_trim_armour_to_tonnage strips points until it is <= designArmourPoints.

designMascMass.doc: MASC: when any slot is 5001 (item table: MASC) the loader sets designMascMass = designMascTons * 100, designMascTons being (designMaxMass / 25 + 50) / 100 - tons / 25 rounded. The recompute adds it.

designRunMP.doc: (walk * 3 + 2) / 2; the ENGINE panel's Running Speed row shows it.

designAmmo.doc: The selected location, 0..7 in MW2 section order (0 head ... 7 left leg). The design's fitted items (sixty-seventh /shell-next; the functions' notes described them by address). Item codes: a weapon is type * 100 + n, n = 1, 2 ... numbering that type's instances; its ammo is 10000 + weapon * 100 + k, k = 1..10. Both lists are packed, unused entries -1.   designAmmo: 25 entries, one ton each (designAmmoMass = 100 per entry); at most     10 per weapon instance. The .mek save turns each into an ammo bin     {10000 + type * 100 + m, weapon}.   designWeapons: 10 entries; designWeaponMass sums itemTypes[code / 100].mass.

mechlabSelectedItem.doc: what the WEAPONS panel has selected: a type from the WEAPONS TABLE (type * 100, n = 0) or a fitted weapon (type * 100 + n), -1 none; ADD WEAPON / ADD AMMO / REMOVE and WEAPON INFO act on it (mechlab_open_weapons_panel clears it)

designCriticals.doc: The design's critical slots, [location][12], 0-based in MW2's section order. The loader copies the MEK's slots in (-1 past numSlots), maps ammo-bin codes (>= 10000) to the design's ammo items, and zeroes the fixed actuators (5301, 5302, 5351, 5352, 5401, 5402, 5451, 5452). The save path (screen_mechlab) writes each entry below 10000 back into MechSection.slots, stopping at -1.

mechlabUnplacedCount.doc: how many entries mechlabUnplaced holds; mechlab_remove_item_slots lowers it.

mechlabUnplaced.doc: First entry of the list of items not yet placed in a location; -1 = none. screen_mechlab's SAVE refuses 'Unassigned criticals detected' otherwise. 78 {item, criticals} pairs; item -1 = empty (mechlab_load_mek's reset writes -1 every 8 bytes up to 0x270). Every 'queue unplaced' in the lab appends {item, slots} at mechlabUnplacedCount, which it keeps below 78 (0x4e). (Was placed as a single int, 'first entry'.)

mechlabTextNormal.doc: screen_mechlab builds its own three text styles the same way: ink -> 6 normal, 1 selected, and 8 warning - then the warning ink per career (0x17 Wolf / Jade Falcon, 0xca career 2). MechlabWidget.textStyle and the draw functions pass them.

mechlabVariants.doc: screen_mechlab's variant list for the current chassis, 200 names of 13 bytes. 0..99: stock '<prefix>NNstd' names that exist in MW2.PRJ (TABL 6); slot 0 is always '<prefix>00std'. 100..199: the player's files 'mek\<prefix>NNusr.mek', slot 100 + NN. Save takes the first free slot from 100 ('Too many mechs of this variant' when none); Delete (user slots only) removes the file and moves on to the next filled slot, wrapping to 0.

mechlabVariant.doc: the selected slot of mechlabVariants: mechlab_load_mek loads it, ACCEPT hands it to star_set_member, and the Delete button is disabled below 100

mechlabForMember.doc: 1 when the mech lab was entered from the star screen for one member (CHANGE MECH or a double click), 0 for its MECH LAB button. screen_mechlab tests it with the previous state 0xd and clears it: when set, ACCEPT MECH assigns the variant to the selected member (star_set_member(-1, ...)) and its button 6 stays disabled; when clear it starts at member 0.

registerSlots.doc: screen_register: the career's ten registry records (slots 0..9 Wolf, 10..19 Jade Falcon), pointers the slot buttons 1..10 index as 0xa6628 + button * 4.

registerCareer.doc: The career whose missions the register lists (careerMissionTables index).

starSlotLayout.doc: screen_star_select points these at the career's tables (career 2: Wolf's).

starPanelLabels.doc: Per panel: the pilot-name, chassis-name and tonnage labels star_slot_draw puts up.

starLimitLabels.doc: star_limits_show: its five labels (formation, mission, maximum 'Mechs, KDMT, total mass), each replaced on a redraw; screen_star_select zeroes them on entry.

layoutRegionFlag.doc: ---- text/briefing/archive (S5) ---- text_layout_page's pending-code flags, static bytes that outlive a call. \Bnnn sets layoutBackPending and \Gnnn layoutColumnPending; the next token read tests them first, clears the flag and re-emits the code as the word "\b%03d" / "\g%03d". \Axx sets layoutRegionFlag; no reader of it has been found (text_layout_page never reads it, and no other function refers to 0xa7170).
